content:
Partition the numbers into 50 triples:
\[
(1,2,3),(4,5,6),\ldots,(148,149,150).
\]
If a chosen set has no three consecutive numbers, it can contain at most 2 numbers from each triple, so at most \(50\cdot 2=100\) marbles can be chosen without forcing three consecutive numbers.

This bound is achievable by choosing
\[
1,2,4,5,7,8,\ldots,148,149,
\]
which has 100 marbles and no three consecutive numbers.

Thus the smallest guaranteed \(n\) is \(100+1=101\).

\[
\boxed{101}
\]
